lines.text: In Lagos, a phone importer sends a thirty percent deposit to a supplier in Shenzhen.
The other seventy percent is still to come. That balance is where it goes wrong.
Goods that never arrive. Payments redirected by a fake "our bank details have changed" message.
A naira that can lose a third of its value between the deposit and the balance.
And letters of credit have almost vanished, so most of this trade moves by plain bank transfer.
Arra fixes that. Arra is Latin for earnest money: the deposit that secures a deal.
Pay the deposit, and keep the balance locked until it ships, in an open contract on Celo: not with Arra, not with the supplier.
Start by describing the order, like a message. Arra's assistant turns it into clear terms.
Words nobody can check, like "good quality", are refused, and the terms are fingerprinted so they can't change later.
Then send your supplier one link. They read the exact terms, in English or Chinese, connect the wallet they want to be paid in, and agree.
No account numbers copied from a chat, so a scammer's look-alike address can't slip in.
Pay in dollars, or straight from naira, even inside MiniPay.
The supplier accepts and gets the deposit instantly. The balance waits until the goods ship.
Every naira payment is a Textile FX fill: a firm quote for exactly the dollars the order needs, settled in one transaction.
Our first one on mainnet turned naira, at about thirteen hundred and seventy-four to the dollar, straight into a locked order.
That one rate matters. In 2023, an importer with a seven-thousand-dollar balance needed two million naira more, just seven weeks later.
With Arra, that balance was paid for on day one.
When the goods arrive, check them. Everything's right? Pay the balance with one tap, all at once or in parts.
Something wrong? Report it with a photo. The supplier accepts, or makes an offer.
Changed your mind before they accept? Cancel and get everything back. If they never accept, or never ship, Arra's agent refunds you automatically.
Silence can't freeze the money, and nobody, not even Arra, can send it anywhere but to the buyer or the supplier.
The same contract works for any deal with a deposit and a balance: a house built back home, furniture made to order, a freelance project.
Arra is live on Celo mainnet. A friend's real order ran start to finish: locked, accepted with the deposit, balance paid.
With a verified contract, a registered agent, and naira orders filled through Textile.
Arra. Trade with anyone, without the worry.
